name: Cost anomaly investigator — attributes what it can and names the gap
_why: The behaviour this agent exists for is the sentence most cost tooling will
not write: 'the idle volumes account for about half of the increase, and
the rest is not explained by anything these two checks can see'.
An investigator that closes that gap with a confident attribution gets
somebody to delete the wrong thing, so the report below is pinned for
saying so out loud. It is also pinned for quoting the automation's own
arithmetic rather than re-deriving it, and for carrying the basis with
every cost estimate — 'published us-east-1 list prices', not the

tools.name: workflow_41
tools.description: Compares account spend per AWS service across two consecutive windows and ranks services by how much they MOVED. Read-only.

tools.name: workflow_42
tools.description: Lists unattached EBS volumes, unassociated elastic IPs and stopped instances in one region, with age, tags and an indicative monthly cost per item. Read-only.

event.input: Our AWS bill jumped this week. Why?

value.restated: Explain the week-on-week increase in the AWS bill and attribute it to resources where possible.
observations_needed: Per-service spend for this week against last week
An inventory of idle resources that could account for a storage increase

script.text: Taking the cost delta and the idle inventory together — neither answers this alone.

script.text: Both returned. I can attribute part of the movement and not all of it.

findings.summary: EC2 - Other rose 182.40 week on week, which is the largest single movement on the bill.
The 38 unattached volumes are a standing cost of roughly 92.40 a month at list price — about half the EC2-Other increase, and not enough to explain it on their own.
Amazon Bedrock is entirely new spend: nothing in the prior window, 74.10 in this one. That is a change somebody made, not waste.

script.text:
**EC2-Other is what moved the bill, and the idle volumes explain about half of it [e:601].**

| Service | Prior | Recent | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EC2 - Other | 410.20 | 592.60 | +182.40 [e:601] |
| Amazon Bedrock | 0.00 | 74.10 | new [e:601] |
| Amazon EC2 | 1204.80 | 1189.30 | -15.50 [e:601] |

Account spend went from 1615.00 to 1856.00, a movement of +241.00 [e:601].

What the inventory accounts for:

- 38 unattached EBS volumes, 3,410 GB in total, at roughly 92.40 a month on published us-east-1 list prices [e:602].
- That is about half the EC2-Other increase. The rest is not explained by anything these two checks can see — EC2-Other also carries snapshots, NAT gateway data processing and provisioned IOPS, and neither tool breaks those out.

Amazon Bedrock is new spend rather than waste: it was not billed at all in the prior window and is 74.10 in this one [e:601]. Somebody turned it on, and they will know why.

Small items, aggregated: 4 unassociated elastic IPs at about 14.40 a month between them [e:602]. Worth reclaiming alongside something else; not worth a change window of their own.

One caveat on the figures: the last day or two of Cost Explorer data are estimates that settle later, and the inventory's costs are list prices rather than your negotiated rate.

Next step: the unattached volumes are a standing cost rather than the cause of this week's movement, so reclaiming them will not reverse it. To close the unexplained remainder you would need spend grouped by usage type rather than by service, which is not something these two automations produce.
